div.head: I Cn 26.4
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe oferhógie, þæt he Godes bodan hlyste, hæbbe him gemæne þæt wið God sylfne.
And se ðe ofærhogie, þæt he Godes bodan hlyste, hæbbe him gemǽne þæt wið God sylfne.
⁊ se þe oferhogyge, þæt he Godes bodan hlyste, hæbbe hym gemæne þæt wið God sylfne.
Et qui Dei preceptis obedire neglexerit, hoc cum ipso Deo commune habeat.
Quicumque autem [de]dignabitur Dei nuncio obaudire, habeat hoc commune cum ipso Deo!
And se ðe ofærhogie þæt he Godes bodan hlyste, hæbbe him gemǽne þæt wið God sylfne.
And se ðe oferhogie, þæt he Godes bodan hlyste, hæbbe him gemæne þæt wið God sylfne.
Und wer auf Gottes Boten zu hören verschmäht, habe das zu verantworten bei Gott selbst!
And whoever scorns to listen to God's messengers, let him settle that with God himself!
And he who disdains to hearken to the messengers of God shall have to settle his case with God himself.
And the person who neglects to heed God’s messengers will have to account for that to God himself.

note.seg: Á sy Godes nama ecelice [-lic Ld] gebletsod ⁊ lof him ⁊ wuldor ⁊ wurðmint symble æfre to worulde [-ld Ld]! Amen. im 16. Jh. am Rande [aus B?] G Ld; vgl. Consil.; ebenso II 84, 5 original; ähnlich Homileten nach Wulfstan 309. 191.

Á sy Godes nama ecelice [-lic Ld] gebletsod ⁊ lof him ⁊ wuldor ⁊ wurðmint symble æfre to worulde [-ld Ld]! Amen. in the margin in the 16th cent. [from B?] G Ld; cf. Consil.; likewise II 84, 5 original; similarly homilists after Wulfstan 309. 191.
Dies benutzen Grið 20; Hom. n. Wulfstan 177 Anm.
This is used by Grið 20; Hom. n. Wulfstan 177 note.
‘Geboten’ Q, als Dat. von bod. Richtig Polity, Homil.: heom, Priester und Bischöfe; s. d. Gl 8a
‘commands’ Q, taking it as dat. of bod. Correctly Polity, Homil.: heom, priests and bishops; see that word in Gl 8a

‘bekomme es mit Gott zu tun, habe eine Verschuldung anhängig bei Gott’ (s. d. Gl 3), öfter in Urkk. Verwünschungsformel gegen Verletzer der Bestimmung, zweimal mit Zusatz ‘im Jüngsten Gericht’; a. 967 Bi 1204; 11. Jh. Thorpe Dipl. 605; Earle Landchar. 273

‘have to reckon with God, have a guilt outstanding before God’ (see that word in Gl 3); frequently in charters as a formula of imprecation against those who infringe the provision, twice with the addition ‘at the Last Judgement’; a. 967 Bi 1204; 11th cent. Thorpe Dipl. 605; Earle Landchar. 273
